<!-- Generated by Ankus.DocGenerator. -->

Namespace: [Ankus](/api/ankus/)

Assembly: `Ankus.Runtime.dll`

Represents a PostgreSQL timestamp with time zone as a UTC instant, including infinities.
PostgreSQL does not retain the original offset or zone name.

```csharp
[JsonConverter(typeof(PgTimestampTzConverter))]
public readonly struct PgTimestampTz : IComparable<PgTimestampTz>, IParsable<PgTimestampTz>, IEquatable<PgTimestampTz>
```

Implements: [IComparable&lt;PgTimestampTz&gt;](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.icomparable-1), [IParsable&lt;PgTimestampTz&gt;](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.iparsable-1), [IEquatable&lt;PgTimestampTz&gt;](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.iequatable-1)

### PgTimestampTz(long)

Creates an instant from microseconds relative to 2000-01-01 UTC. Int64 extremes represent infinities.

### AtTimeZone(PgInterval)

Converts this instant to a local timestamp at a fixed interval offset from UTC.

```csharp
public PgTimestamp AtTimeZone(PgInterval offset)
```

Parameters:

`offset` — [PgInterval](/api/ankus.pginterval/)

A finite interval without months or days; positive values mean east of UTC.

Returns: [PgTimestamp](/api/ankus.pgtimestamp/)

The local timestamp, preserving infinities according to PostgreSQL's rules.

Requires the active backend thread. Offset precision and invalid-interval handling follow
PostgreSQL's interval form of AT TIME ZONE.

### TryParse(string?, out PgTimestampTz)

Tries to parse PostgreSQL timestamp syntax on the active backend thread.

```csharp
public static bool TryParse(string? text, out PgTimestampTz value)
```

Parameters:

`text` — [string](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.string)

The timestamp text.

`value` — [PgTimestampTz](/api/ankus.pgtimestamptz/)

The parsed instant, or the default value on invalid input.

Returns: [bool](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.boolean)

Whether the input is valid. Backend-access and operational errors still throw.

Invalid input leaves no error pending: PostgreSQL 16 and later report it as a soft input error, and earlier majors
roll back an internal subtransaction. Before PostgreSQL 16, transaction callbacks and parallel operations forbid
that rollback; native errors there remain pending and throw PgException.
